references.text: God asks a question of the human being, even though he already knows the answer. Here God asks Adam, "Where are you?", in the same way that he asks Balaam about who the men are.
God asks Cain the question, "Where is your brother Abel?" This is a similar rhetorical question where God confronts the human being.
God comes to Abimelech in a dream at night, in a similar manner as God comes to Balaam.
God comes to Laban the Aramean in a dream at night, which shows God's pattern of revealing himself to non-Israelites.
God comes again to Balaam at night, as a continuation of this first revelation.
God meets Balaam again later in the story, showing the continued pattern of divine communication.
God asks Satan a question about where he comes from, a similar rhetorical question where God already knows the answer.
Again God asks Satan a question he already knows the answer to, as a parallel to the question asked of Balaam.
